artist.name: Anson Seabra
artist.place_of_origin: Blue Springs, Missouri, United States (raised; Kansas City area)
artist.short_description: Missouri-raised pianist and songwriter combining storybook imagery with emotional singer-songwriter pop.
artist.biography: Anson Seabra, whose full name is Anson Long-Seabra, is an American singer-songwriter associated with the Kansas City area of Missouri. He studied computer science at Truman State University and began his career as a software engineer before choosing music as a full-time pursuit. His university's alumni profile details that change and the online attention surrounding his 2018 recording 'Welcome to Wonderland'. Seabra has since built a catalogue of piano-centered, narrative pop, often combining ordinary emotional struggles with fantastical images. In an interview with EnVi, he described the significance of Ruth B.'s 'Lost Boy' as an influence on 'Welcome to Wonderland', particularly its combination of nostalgia and escapism. His album 'Songs I Wrote in My Bedroom' arrived in 2020, followed by the project 'Feeling For My Life' in 2021, which explored vulnerability and changing perspectives. In a separate first-person interview, Seabra connected 'Broken' and 'Lucky Charms' to difficult personal periods and reflections on self-worth. His later releases include 'Peter Pan Was Right' in 2022 and the album 'A Heart Is a Terrible Thing to Break' in 2023. Afterglow categorizes his work as emotional piano-pop and narrative singer-songwriter music; this is editorial language rather than an exhaustive official genre label. His profile also expands the site's selection of male-vocal emotional pop alongside Caleb Hearn.
